bull.b: Zero reported TTM debt provides lasting financial flexibility for a clinical-stage biopharma. With no interest burden, management can prioritize R&D and trial funding choices, extending runway via equity instead of debt and preserving cash flow available for operations and partnerships.

bull.t: Strong gross margins on product sales
bull.b: Reported low-70% gross margins on the limited revenue base point to attractive unit economics for antibody/protein products. If the company advances candidates to commercial scale, these structural margins can support profitable operations once fixed R&D and SG&A are absorbed.

Shareholder-approved authority to issue shares through mid-2029 gives the board durable access to equity financing, a critical tool for clinical-stage firms. This structural capacity reduces dependence on short-term bridge debt and enables planned funding of trials and partnerships over multiple years.

bear.b: Sustained operating and free cash outflows (~$27M TTM) are a long-term structural constraint for a pre-revenue/low-revenue biotech. Continued negative cash flow necessitates recurrent financing, limits strategic optionality, and can force prioritization or delay of clinical programs absent new capital.

Very low recurring revenue (~$0.5M TTM) alongside substantial net losses (~$35.7M TTM) indicates the company remains in an investment phase with no near-term profit backbone. This structural disconnect increases reliance on external funding until products reach commercialization.

A falling equity base over recent years signals repeated financing and cumulative losses, eroding the balance-sheet buffer. Combined with ongoing cash burn and authority to issue shares, this trend raises durable dilution and capital-availability concerns for funding future development.
